scope.note: No tag was created and nothing was pushed or published; --tag v0.8.0 is a local packaging argument matching Cargo.toml's committed version.

steps.description: Confirm the workspace version matches the tag under rehearsal.
Rebuild the release binary locked and offline against the current working tree (already up to date; no recompilation needed).
Verify the current tool snapshots against the committed 0.8.0 freeze manifest before packaging.
Build the deterministic core archive, inventory, SPDX SBOM and third-party notices from the built binary.
Compare the generated archive size against the archive_size_core_bytes budget (12.7 MB).
Copy the archive and SHA256SUMS into a fresh clean directory under target/, simulating a clean download separate from the build output directory.

First smoke attempt from the clean-download directory failed closed: two tools' pinned combined-schema hashes in release-smoke.py's TOOL_SCHEMA_SHA256 did not match the live tools/list response, even though the same tools' per-field hashes (description/input/output schema, annotations) matched both `contract --json` and the committed freeze manifest exactly. This is a real bug in the verifier's pinned constants, not a contract regression.
steps.excerpt: ValueError: tool schemas differ from the frozen contract: rust.binary.bloat

steps.description: Fixed the two mis-pinned TOOL_SCHEMA_SHA256 entries in scripts/release-smoke.py (rust.binary.bloat, rust.analyzer.action.apply) by recomputing sha256(canonical_json({inputSchema, outputSchema})) from a live tools/list response, cross-checked against contract --json and the freeze manifest.

Re-ran the smoke test from the same clean-download directory after the fix: extracts, verifies SHA-256 against SHA256SUMS, installs into an ephemeral 0700 directory, runs --version/version --json/doctor --json, then serve --stdio with tools/list (36, exact hash match) and four representative tools/call requests, tears down and confirms no leaked process group.
Regression guard: full release-smoke.py unit test suite after the fix.

Extracted the clean-download archive to a manual install directory and ran `version --json`, `doctor --json` and `contract --json` directly against the archived binary (independent of release-smoke.py's own install/verify path).
steps.excerpt: version.version=0.8.0; doctor.mode=passive,status=warning; contract.tool_count=36, per-tool description/input/output schema hashes and annotations match docs/validation/M8/freeze-0.8.0.json for all 36 tools

steps.description: Manual MCP stdio session against the extracted binary: server/discover, tools/list, resources/templates/list.
steps.excerpt: tools/list: 36 tools (name set matches freeze manifest); resources/templates/list: 2 templates (rust-artifact://{project_ref}/{artifact_id}, rust-quality-artifact://{project_ref}/{quality_job_id_or_artifact_id}?offset={n}&length={n})

steps.description: Cleanup: removed the local rehearsal scratch directory under target/ (clean-download copies, manual install, helper scripts).

found_and_fixed.issue: TOOL_SCHEMA_SHA256["rust.binary.bloat"] and TOOL_SCHEMA_SHA256["rust.analyzer.action.apply"] held stale combined inputSchema/outputSchema hashes that did not match the live tools/list response, even though every per-field hash (description/input/output schema) and every annotation for those same tools matched both `contract --json` and docs/validation/M8/freeze-0.8.0.json exactly.
found_and_fixed.detected_by: step 7 (release-smoke.py failing closed during the clean-download rehearsal)
found_and_fixed.fix: Recomputed the correct combined hashes from a live tools/list response and replaced both constants.
found_and_fixed.verified_by: steps 9 and 10 (smoke passes; full test-release-smoke.py suite passes)
